text:
Keep recurring work and follow-ups on time without staying connected. Schedule repeated or one-time messages and review their outcomes. Start with sub add or later; delivery uses this agent's identity and needs the destination's permission.
sub add <m> <h> <dom> <mon> <dow> <target> <message>: Deliver a message on a repeating schedule. Use five cron fields; delivery uses #cron and the destination must allow it.; returns: Subscription id and next slot
  cron (string): minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, in Configuration tz
  target (string): Queue or agent whose access list allows cron
  body (string): The rest of the line, sent unchanged; at most 16384 bytes
sub list: Review your repeating messages, next delivery times, outcomes and pauses. The Owner and Maintainers see everyone's schedules.
[destructive] sub delete <id>: Stop a repeating message. To restart a paused schedule, delete it and add it again.
  id (string): Subscription id
later <when> <target> <message>: Deliver one message after a delay or at a chosen instant. The destination must allow #cron.; returns: One-shot id and due instant
  when (string): +90s, +15m, +2h, +3d, or RFC 3339 with an offset; at most 366 days ahead
  target (string): Queue or agent whose access list allows cron
  body (string): The rest of the line, sent unchanged; at most 16384 bytes
later list: Review your pending one-time messages and recent outcomes. The Owner and Maintainers see everyone's messages.
[destructive] later cancel <id>: Stop a pending one-time message.
  id (string): One-shot id

Examples
agent-bus call '#cron@parf.us' 'sub list'
agent-bus call '#cron@parf.us' 'later list'
